title: So Purakh: that Being
hookLine: so purakh niranjan: that Being is pure, beyond reach, and all meditate on Him (Asa M4, ang 10–11)

lines: A PLATE HELD OVER A LAMP.
SOOT: THE OLD WAY TO MAKE KAJAL.
cards: Kajal, the black eyeliner, can be made at home by an old method. You light a small oil lamp and hold a clay or brass plate just above the flame. In a few minutes the underside is coated in soft black soot.
Scrape it off, mix it with a little ghee, and you have kajal. The flame itself stays bright and clean. Everything it touches turns black.
That old word for soot and eyeliner, anjan, is hiding inside today's line.

teach.h: SO PURAKH: GURU RAM DAS'S SHABADS.
teach.b: Rehras has two more shabads in its first group, and we'll come back to them in a few days. Today we jump to the second group, called So Purakh after its opening words. The voice changes too.
These are by Guru Ram Das, the fourth Guru. It opens: so purakh niranjan. That Being, purakh, is niranjan.
Nir means without. Anjan is that soot, the black of kajal, and so a stain.

teach.h: NIRANJAN: WITHOUT A STAIN, NO SOOT.
teach.b: Niranjan: without a stain. Untouched by the soot of the world, the way the flame stays clean while the plate turns black. The line goes on: the Lord, beyond reach, beyond reach, without limit.

teach.h: ALL MEDITATE ON YOU, GIVER OF ALL.
teach.b: Then, in paraphrase: all meditate on You, all meditate on You, true Creator. All beings are Yours, and You are the giver to every being. Meditate on the Lord, saints; He takes away every sorrow.

teach.h: HIMSELF THE MASTER, HIMSELF THE SERVANT.
teach.b: And then a line that turns everything inward: the Lord Himself is the master, and the Lord Himself is the servant. What is poor Nanak?
Guru Ram Das signs with the name Nanak, as the Gurus whose hymns are in the Guru Granth Sahib do. Notice the repeating. Beyond reach, beyond reach.
All meditate, all meditate. The words circle, the way a lamp flame flickers but stays a flame. In kirtan, So Purakh can be sung slowly, the lines doubling back.
The picture it leaves at dusk is simple: whatever soot the day has left on you, that Being is untouched by it.

how: So Purakh is the first of four shabads in the second group of Rehras Sahib, recited each evening; in kirtan it can be sung slowly, its doubled phrases repeated.

o: that Being, pure and beyond reach
the first human being, father of all
a holy man who has given up the world

s: So Purakh was written by Guru Nanak
it is by Guru Ram Das, the fourth Guru, who signs with the name Nanak.
nir, without; anjan, soot or kajal.
the shabad says the Lord is Himself both master and servant
and asks: what is poor Nanak?

games.q: Guru Ram Das calls that Being niranjan. what picture is inside the word?
o: a mountain no one can climb.
a flame with no soot on it: without a stain.
games.why: anjan is soot, the black of kajal; niranjan is without it, untouched by the world's stain.

practice: Say so purakh niranjan three times, slowly, out loud or under your breath.

Then let the words go and picture a lamp flame, steady and clean while the plate above it gathers soot, and let the day's smudges be on the plate, not the flame. If you pray, you can end with Waheguru.

wordCard.voice: So Purakh. That Being: the opening of Guru Ram Das's shabads in Rehras. So purakh niranjan: that Being is without stain, beyond reach, the giver of all.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: niranjan, without stain; from nir, without, and anjan, soot or kajal.

carryVoice: Your line: pure being. Nir, without; anjan, the soot of the lamp. Day four hundred nine, done.

sources.ref: Asa M4, so purakh niranjan, Ang 10–11
